headline: Oil markets plunge and copper slumps as AI and geopolitical fears hit demand
paragraphs: Brent crude suffered its steepest weekly drop since 2020, tumbling nearly seventeen percent as markets reacted to growing hopes for Middle East diplomacy and shifting sentiment. WTI crude followed suit with a weekly decline exceeding thirteen percent. The euro traded at 1.1228 against the dollar, helping cushion import costs for Irish businesses.

Copper fell toward multi-month lows, heading for its worst week since March amid a sharp rout in the artificial intelligence sector and concerns over shifting United States trade policy. Meanwhile, precious metals posted solid weekly gains despite slight daily pullbacks, with gold holding above the critical four thousand dollar threshold ahead of key United States jobs data, though a hawkish Federal Reserve and strong employment figures threaten further recovery. Palladium dropped nearly two percent on the day to close at one thousand twenty-one dollars and fifty cents.
